Article Title: Gold price prediction today: What levels will yellow metal see? Check outlook for October 12, 2026 week
Article Text:
Importantly, underlying investment demand for bullion remains strong, with inflows into gold-backed ETFs reaching a four-year high

Gold price prediction today

:

Gold prices are recovering, but are continuing to see pressure due to global factors, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.

Here’s his analysis:

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Gold enters the week Rs 150,750 after recovering from the recent decline towards Rs 146,000–147,000, although prices remain well below the September peak near Rs 163,000–165,000. The daily structure has improved modestly, with gold moving back above the 20-day average near Rs 150,263, suggesting that selling pressure is stabilising after the recent correction.Bollinger Bands show the upper band near Rs 155,047 and lower band around Rs 145,480, leaving prices close to the middle of the range. From a broader perspective, repeated ability to hold the Rs 145,000-147,000 region keeps medium-term structure constructive despite recent volatility. Immediate support is placed around Rs 149,000–150,000, followed by the stronger Rs 145,500-147,000 zone.A sustained break below Rs 145,000 would weaken the broader setup and could expose Rs 140,000–142,000. On the upside, Rs 152,500-153,000 remains the first hurdle, followed by the upper Bollinger region around Rs 155,000.A sustained move above Rs 155,000 could strengthen momentum and open the way towards Rs 158,000–160,000, followed by September high around Rs 163,000–165,000.Overall, near-term bias remains neutral to mildly positive, while the one-to-three-month structure continues to look constructive as long as Rs 145,000 holds. A breakout above Rs 155,000 would provide stronger confirmation that the recent corrective phase is ending and that the broader upward move is resuming.Gold ended the week higher and enters the new week with a constructive undertone as easing energy prices and strengthening investment demand offset pressure from elevated Treasury yields and expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. Crude oil declined after the US and Iran reached an energy truce, helping moderate immediate concerns over another energy-driven inflation shock, although broader Middle East uncertainty continues to support safe-haven demand.More importantly, underlying investment demand for bullion remains strong, with inflows into gold-backed ETFs reaching a four-year high as investors increasingly focus on rising fiscal deficits, government debt-servicing costs and longer-term currency debasement risks.Central-bank accumulation also continues to provide structural support, with the People’s Bank of China adding around 740,000 ounces of gold during September, extending its buying streak to 23 consecutive months. However, the monetary-policy backdrop remains a significant headwind.Persistent inflationary pressures have kept the possibility of additional Fed tightening alive, supporting nominal and real Treasury yields and increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.Gold therefore remains caught between two powerful forces: elevated yields and tighter monetary-policy expectations limiting near-term upside, while ETF inflows, central-bank accumulation, fiscal concerns and geopolitical uncertainty support the broader bullish structure.For the week ahead, Treasury yields, Fed communication, crude oil and geopolitical developments are likely to determine whether gold can extend its recovery towards recent highs.
Article Summary: Gold prices are recovering, but are continuing to see pressure due to global factors, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. Immediate support is placed around Rs 149,000–150,000, followed by the stronger Rs 145,500-147,000 zone.

Article Title: Sunil Bharti Mittal gets highest French civilian award
Article Text:
Sunil Bharti Mittal

NEW DELHI: Sunil Bharti Mittal, Bharti Enterprises founder and chairman, has been named a Chevalier de l’Ordre national de la Légion d’Honneur (Knight of the National Order of the Legion of Honour) by French President Emmanuel Macron.Established in 1802 by Napoleon Bonaparte, the Légion d’Honneur is the highest civilian award bestowed by the French Republic. Mittal has been conferred the distinction in recognition of his longstanding commitment to deepening economic ties between India and France, and his outstanding achievements in telecommunications and digital infrastructure.Ambassador Thierry Mathou said: “Sunil Bharti Mittal has been a friend of France for more than thirty years, since the early days of Airtel in 1992. He has unflaggingly nurtured these ties over the decades, and shown what French and Indian business endeavours can achieve together. Today he advances these relations as Vice-Chairman of Eutelsat, at a time when our two countries are moving forward jointly in space and digital technology. In awarding him the Légion d’honneur, the President of the Republic recognises an outstanding business leader who has contributed to making France a lasting partner in India.”Mittal said: “I am moved and humbled by this gracious award from the Republic of France. My association with France began at Airtel’s inception in 1992, when Compagnie Générale des Eaux joined hands with Bharti to introduce mobile telephony in India. It continues today through my role as Co-Chairman of Eutelsat, the European satellite champion. I accept this honour with gratitude to the President of the French Republic, Emmamuel Macron and with a renewed commitment to further deepen the economic ties between India and France. ”The insignia will be conferred at a ceremony to be held on Wednesday (Oct 28) at the embassy of France in India, New Delhi.In 2007, Mittal was conferred the Padma Bhushan, one of India’s highest civilian honours. In 2024, he became the first Indian citizen to be honoured as a Knight Commander of the Most Excellent Order of the British Empire (KBE) by King Charles III.
Article Summary: Sunil Bharti Mittal named a Chevalier de l’Ordre national de la Légion d’Honneur by French President Emmanuel Macron. Mittal has been conferred the distinction in recognition of his longstanding commitment to deepening economic ties between India and France.

Article Title: Indian rice exporters move 102,210 tonnes Basmati rice across three vessels to Iraq
Article Text: NEW DELHI: India's rice exporters have arranged shipments of 102,210 metric tonnes of Basmati rice to Iraq across three bulk vessels, aiming to cut freight costs by 74% amid shipping disruptions, container shortages and rising logistics expenses.The Indian Rice Exporters' Federation (IREF), in collaboration with Singapore-based Eximwala Solutions Pte. Ltd., said the arrangement would bring freight costs down to around $90 per tonne, compared with container-shipping quotations of about $350 per tonne. This would mean a potential saving of $260 per tonne.Based on these quoted rates, the three-vessel programme could generate gross freight savings of about $26.6 million. The actual savings, however, would depend on the final shipping costs and contractual terms.The three vessels are bound for Iraq's Umm Qasr port. The MV LAMAR S, carrying 36,810 tonnes of rice, has reached the port, berthed at Berth No. 3 and begun unloading its cargo, IREF said.The other two vessels: MV LOLO GATE and MV OUTLANDER, have been nominated to carry 25,500 tonnes and 39,900 tonnes, respectively.The initiative comes as exporters face higher freight rates and logistical uncertainty affecting shipments to the Gulf, India's largest regional market for Basmati rice.India exported 4.564 million tonnes of Basmati rice worth Rs 34,284 crore to the Middle East in the financial year ended March 2026, accounting for around 70% of its total Basmati export volume, according to figures cited by IREF.Including non-Basmati varieties, India's rice exports to the region stood at 5.648 million tonnes, valued at Rs 39,657 crore.Saudi Arabia was India's largest Basmati market in the region, with imports worth Rs 8,324 crore in FY2025-26. It was followed by Iran at Rs 6,970 crore, Iraq at Rs 5,583 crore and the United Arab Emirates at Rs 4,132 crore, the federation said.Iraq imported around 764,000 tonnes of Indian Basmati rice during the period, highlighting the importance of competitive freight rates and reliable shipping routes for exporters."The Middle East accounts for nearly 70 per cent of India's Basmati exports, and rising shipping costs directly affect our competitiveness. By targeting a reduction in freight from USD 350 to USD 90 per tonne, we are demonstrating how better logistics can benefit both Indian exporters and overseas buyers. Our objective is to develop similar commercially viable solutions for other Gulf destinations, strengthen India's rice exports and improve returns across the value chain," Dev Garg, national vice president of IREF said, PTI reported.Lower freight costs could help exporters protect profit margins and keep their rice competitively priced in overseas markets. Bulk shipments may also provide an alternative when containers are scarce or expensive.However, the benefits will depend on the availability of bulk vessels, port-handling charges, shipment schedules and whether bulk transport suits individual consignments and buyers.The initiative comes ahead of the Bharat International Rice Conference (BIRC) 2026, scheduled to be held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi from October 23 to 25.
Article Summary: India's rice exporters have arranged shipments of 102,210 metric tonnes of Basmati rice to Iraq across three bulk vessels. The three-vessel programme could generate gross freight savings of about $26.6 million. The initiative comes as exporters face higher freight rates and logistical uncertainty.

Driven by rising demand for skill-based education, Renu continues to expand CoachX’s footprint through hybrid learning centres across India, making career-focused learning more accessible nationwide.Suraj Dubey, a Surat-based optometrist and founder of Sleepaxa , is translating clinical experience into research-led eyewear innovation. Since 2017, he has conducted over 10,000 eye examinations, inspiring his exploration of how light influences visual comfort and well-being. Through Acieon Labs, he leads research behind wavelength-selective lenses, supported by two granted Indian patents NeuroCalm FLX+ and Circadian560. Sleepaxa allocates approximately 30% of its budget to innovation and patent filings. Guided by “evidence over myths,” Suraj combines entrepreneurship, scientific inquiry and public education to build a homegrown brand focused on purposeful innovation for modern lifestyles.Together, these visionary leaders reflect the evolving spirit of Indian enterprise, where innovation, resilience and purpose drive meaningful progress. Across industries, their journeys demonstrate how entrepreneurial ambition can create lasting value, empower communities and address emerging challenges, contributing to a more sustainable, inclusive and progressive India.
Article Summary: Aakriti Sunder, Aditya Pittie, Apoorv Agarwal, Chetan Suvarna, Anjini Sharma, Suraj Dubey and Renu Salgarkar are some of India's leading business leaders. They are transforming industries, creating meaningful impact and contributing to a stronger, more progressive India.

Article Title: Five Bangalore landowners faced tax on rental income from an IT park built through a partnership firm; IT department alleged it was a tax-avoidance structure, ITAT gives relief
Article Text:
In 1999, five landowners decided to develop their property into an IT park and SEZ zone. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the landowners win the case?

What constitutes tax avoidance? In a recent ruling, five Bangalore landowners have secured relief from ITAT in an income tax dispute over alleged undisclosed rental income.They established that the building belonged to their partnership firm, which received rent directly into its bank account, filed income tax returns and paid taxes on the earnings.In 1999, five landowners decided to develop their property into an IT park and SEZ zone. To take the project forward, they signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with a builder.Also Read | He bought a Rs 41.85 lakh and paid Rs 39.15 lakh but did not get possession; builder blames PMC-PMRDA jurisdiction changes, MahaRERA rejects excuse and orders interest payout to homebuyer In 2005, the landowners and the same builder executed a registered joint development agreement (JDA). Under the arrangement, the builder was granted development rights and a Power of Attorney (POA) was executed for various purposes. The builder also paid the landowners a refundable, interest-free deposit of Rs 37.25 lakh.As part of the development, the builder was to construct a separate C1 Block for SEZ activities. He subsequently set up a partnership firm to manage the block, retaining a 96% stake while the landowners collectively held the remaining 4%.Once the construction was completed, the firm leased the premises to several companies.The rental payments were credited directly to its bank account.The partnership firm also filed its income tax returns and paid tax on its earnings. Meanwhile, the landowners made withdrawals from the firm in the usual course.The C1 Block was constructed and allotted to the landowners in AY 2016-17. They also paid the BBMP tax relating to the block.The arrangement continued without any apparent dispute until 2022, when the Income Tax Department conducted a search at a company associated with the landowners' family. The findings from the operation triggered a series of disputes.Also Read | Man invested Rs 10 lakh, which tax department treated as unexplained; he first cited cash loan, then bank withdrawals as source, ITAT Nagpur deletes addition and Rs 2.11 lakh penalty At the centre of the tax controversy was the commercial property in Block C1, developed under the 2005 JDA.The Assessing Officer (AO) of the Income Tax Department took the position that the landowners, rather than the partnership firm, were the property's actual owners.The AO consequently viewed the firm as an arrangement designed to evade tax, maintaining that the landowners were the real owners of Block C1.The AO cited, among other reasons, withdrawals made by the landowner families that were not proportionate to their declared 4% profit-sharing entitlement. The officer also alleged that the partnership deed had not been registered.On this basis, the AO sought to assess the rental earnings from Block C1 directly in the hands of the landowners and their family members, instead of the partnership firm. The Commissioner of Appeals (CIT(A)) agreed with this position and upheld the assessment approach.The landowners subsequently challenged the decision before the Bangalore bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) and won relief.Also Read | Landlords wanted tenant out to open a law office; he said the reason for seeking eviction had changed and other properties were available, why Delhi High Court upheld eviction Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that the ITAT Bangalore relied on substantial documentary evidence to establish that the partnership firm was a genuine business entity.Government and statutory authorities had recognised it as a co-developer of the SEZ, while infrastructure and electricity approvals were issued in its name. Its audited financial statements also reflected the rental earnings, and tenants paid rent directly into the firm's bank account.Surana highlighted that the Income-tax Department had itself assessed the partnership firm in previous years and accepted the rental income reported in its returns.The tribunal also dismissed the department's contention that withdrawals made by the landowner partners established that the rental earnings had actually accrued to them personally.According to the ITAT Bangalore, amounts taken out by partners are ordinarily entered in the partnership firm's books as debits to their respective capital accounts.Surana says: “Such withdrawals do not, merely for that reason, become fresh rental income in the partners' hands, nor do they transfer ownership of the underlying property from the firm to the partners.”Also Read | Woman buys Rs 1.03 crore 3BHK in Bengaluru, but builder fails to provide specially-enabled parking; Karnataka RERA orders provision within 60 days and audited maintenance accounts The tribunal further pointed out that one of the taxpayers involved in the dispute was not a partner in the firm at all and had received no money from it.Separately, the ITAT examined the capital gains issue arising from the JDA. The Assessing Officer (AO) had proposed taxing the gains in AY 2016-17, arguing that the builder had completed the construction and handed over the developed area to the landowners during that year.The landowners maintained that the taxable transfer had taken place much earlier, when they signed the registered JDA and executed the Power of Attorney in March 2005, thereby placing effective control of the property with the builder.On examining the agreement, the tribunal found that the developer had been granted extensive and irrevocable rights from the beginning. These included access to the property, securing approvals, designing and developing the project, signing agreements with purchasers and mortgaging the property to arrange finance. The registered Power of Attorney (POA) had also vested broad authority in the developer.Based on these provisions, the ITAT Bangalore concluded that the transfer had already taken place in AY 2005-06, around the time the JDA and POA were executed. Consequently, the transfer could not be treated as having occurred in AY 2016-17 merely because the completed area was handed over to the landowners during that year.Ultimately, the taxpayers succeeded in all their appeals, with the disputed additions being deleted. The landowners secured the favourable ruling from the Bangalore ITAT on August 27, 2026.
Article Summary: In 1999, five landowners decided to develop their property into an IT park and SEZ zone. In 2005, the landowners and the same builder executed a registered joint development agreement (JDA) The arrangement continued without any apparent dispute until 2022, when the Income Tax Department conducted a search at a company associated with the landowners' family.

Article Title: Goyal backs global growth push for Indian startups; Gajwani flags AI gap
Article Text:
(L to R) Anshul Agrawal and Saurabh Bothra of Habuild; Ayush Ranjan, Prateesh Awasthi and Vishrant Dave of Armatrix; Mukund Jha of Emergent; Manu Chandra of Sauce; Pallavi Mohadikar of Palmonas; Pallavi Shrivastava of Progcap; commerce minister Piyush Goyal; Times Internet chairman Satyan Gajwani; ETSA juror Aryaman Vikram Birla of Aditya Birla Group; Lalit Keshre and Ishan Bansal of Groww; Peddi Shanmukh Srinivas, Ambarish Ghosh and Debayan Dasgupta of Theranautilus; and Trishala Bothra of Habuild

ET 2026: Startup Awards

Winners of ET Startup Awards 2026

BENGALURU: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal called on Indian start-ups to look beyond the domestic market and expand overseas, offering govt funding to showcase them at international exhibitions and conferences. He said a sustained three-to-five-year push could help startups tap new markets and attract investors. Goyal also argued that tighter H-1B visa access could benefit India by retaining talent and bringing more work to the country’s global capability centres.“We are willing to fund whatever it takes to take our startups to the rest of the world,” Goyal said at the ET Startup Awards 2026 in Bengaluru on Friday. “Let’s get out of the cozy comfort of the large Indian opportunity or Indian market. Let us think of going global,” he added.Times Internet chairman Satyan Gajwani flagged India’s lag in artificial intelligence, saying the country needs deeper research, greater computing power and patient capital to close the gap with the US and China.“As the US and China race ahead in artificial intelligence, India’s progress has been slower than it should be,” Gajwani said. He also added that India is witnessing a maturing startup ecosystem, with founders increasingly focused on deep, proprietary technology.Citing the launch of Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket, he said the achievement signalled the growing capabilities of Indian startups in deep tech. “Indian startups are now building semiconductor chips, AI robotics, clean energy technologies and new materials while investors are shaping funds willing to wait longer for these companies to mature,” Gajwani said.He attributed this shift to entrepreneurial ambition, founders turning investors and govt support. “This maturing of the Indian startup ecosystem, this energy and this audacity, founders paying it forward as investors, the structural backing by the state — they’ve all come together thanks to a lot of advocacy and championing by many of our leaders,” he said. India has grown from a few hundred recognised startups to more than 2.5 lakh, creating close to 25 lakh jobs, Gajwani added.Moderating a panel on India’s deep tech ambitions, Accel India founding partner Prashanth Prakash said building such companies required infrastructure and regulatory changes beyond those needed for conventional software businesses. “To build deep tech we need all these enabling elements that were not required for just a software company,” he said.Agrani Labs cofounder and CEO Dheemanth Nagaraj, whose company is developing AI GPUs for data centres, said Indian products had to compete globally on quality. “There is no space for building a substandard product at a lower cost,” he said. Govt could help create a market by becoming a first customer, he added.Spacetech firm Pixxel cofounder and CTO Kshitij Khandelwal said reforms had eased satellite licensing, but setting up manufacturing facilities remained challenging. “The issues that we have faced mostly are local in nature,” he said.BrainSight AI cofounder and CEO Laina Emmanuel said mapping brain function requires complex science and significant computing power. “It’s hard science, it’s hard tech, it’s hard market building for us,” she said.At a panel on the journey to listing, Meesho CEO Vidit Aatrey recalled retired investors at the company’s first annual general meeting, telling him they were investing savings accumulated over their lifetimes. “Now you are responsible for their money, and you have to behave differently,” he said.Groww CEO Lalit Keshre said the listing strengthened the connection between the company and its users, many of whom also became shareholders. The company continued to pursue its long-term goals through regular reviews. “The philosophy is that you think long term, but you execute short term.”
Article Summary: commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal called on Indian start-ups to look beyond the domestic market and expand overseas. He said a sustained three-to- five-year push could help startups tap new markets and attract investors. Times Internet chairman Satyan Gajwani flagged India’s lag in artificial intelligence.

Article Title: Manipur on edge after fresh killings; 9 killed in 12 hours, shutdowns disrupt key highways
Article Text:
CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh condemned the killings of civilians and appealed for restraint and dialogue.





GUWAHATI: Manipur ’s hill districts remained tense on Sunday after nine people were killed in 12 hours of ethnic violence across Kamjong, Kangpokpi and Ukhrul districts on Saturday.Additional security forces were deployed in the affected areas of Kangpokpi and Kamjong districts, while separate shutdowns disrupted traffic on National Highways 2 and 202.The Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) called a 24-hour strike from Saturday evening. The Kuki CSOs Working Committee, Ukhrul, also enforced a shutdown in Ukhrul over the killings and its allegations of involvement by Naga militants and security personnel. No fresh fatality was reported on Sunday.CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh condemned the killings of civilians and appealed for restraint and dialogue. “CM has instructed the authorities concerned to take immediate and effective steps to tackle the situation, restore peace and order, and ensure the safety and security of all citizens,” the CM’s office said.The Kuki Chiefs’ Association, Manipur (KCA-M), on Sunday condemned what it called a “pre-planned attack” on unarmed civilian protesters in Chassad Kuki village in Kamjong district on Oct 9 and 10. It alleged that cadres of the NSCN (I-M), NSCN (Eastern Flank) and ZUF-K, in collusion with Tangkhul IRB personnel posted in the district, carried out the attack.“In this cowardly attack, the armed groups opened fire on civilian protesters and burnt down houses in Chassad village, resulting in the killing of Domkhonei Touthang and Michael Ngamminlen Haokip, both innocent Kuki civilians of Chassad village, and the destruction of houses,” the KCA-M said in a statement.The association claimed that the latest incidents took the number of Kuki civilian victims killed in attacks allegedly led by Tangkhul-led NSCN groups since March 11 this year to 30.The KCA-M demanded the immediate registration of FIRs for murder, arson and criminal conspiracy against the alleged perpetrators and the “involved IRB personnel”, along with their arrest. It also sought ex gratia payments of Rs 30 lakh each and govt jobs for the next of kin of the deceased, besides full compensation and the urgent reconstruction of the burnt houses.“Centre and security forces must understand the ground reality and secure all Kuki villages in Kamjong, Ukhrul, Tamenglong and Noney districts with adequate deployment of central forces to prevent further attacks,” the KCA-M said. It reiterated its demand for a separate union territory with a legislature for the Kuki-Zo people under the Constitution, saying this was necessary for lasting peace and security.The 12-hour outbreak of violence claimed six Naga lives, two Kuki lives — including that of a mother of five — and the life of a Gorkha farmer. Gunfights and arson targeting homes and shops were reported across the three districts, marking one of Manipur’s deadliest outbreaks of violence in the past year.Meanwhile, the working committee of the Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL), the apex traditional body of the Tangkhul Naga community, condemned the attacks on Tangkhul Naga civilians and alleged repeated aggression against border villages in Kamjong.“The external aggression against the border Naga villagers of Kamjong by the Kuki war parties has become a routine affair since the outbreak of violent conflict in the hills of Manipur,” it said.“In spite of the grim and alarming situation along the India-Myanmar border, the current political dispensation at Imphal and New Delhi has become a helpless spectator to the cross-border terrorism, while wilfully leaving their innocent citizens at the mercy of the foreign aggressors,” the organisation alleged.The TNL urged the authorities to take measures to protect residents living along Kamjong district’s porous international border.
Article Summary: Nine people were killed in 12 hours of ethnic violence across Kamjong, Kangpokpi and Ukhrul districts on Saturday. The 12-hour outbreak of violence claimed six Naga lives, two Kuki lives — including that of a mother of five — and the life of a Gorkha farmer.

Article Title: ‘Abhijeet Dipke? Detained. Vijeta Dahiya? Out!’ Ex-CJP spokesperson mocks party leaders; watch
Article Text:
Vijeta Dahiya publicly mocked Dhruv Rathee, Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and Ashutosh Ranka after they were detained.

CJP had removed Dahiya as spokesperson

Over 3,000 detained ahead of CJP protest





NEW DELHI: Former Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya on Saturday mocked party founder Abhijeet Dipke, co-convenor Saurav Das , leader Ashutosh Ranka and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee after they were detained by Delhi Police ahead of a planned protest at Jantar Mantar.In a video posted on Instagram, Dahiya listed the four names, saying each has been detained, before contrasting their fate with his own: “But Vijeta Dahiya? Out!” He followed it with a teasing gesture and bursts out laughing.“Zyada load mat lo (don’t overthink it),” he said, adding that he was heading out just to recite a poem about protest and raise a few slogans. He then told Delhi Police to stop chasing and detaining protesters and arrest criminals instead.“Delhi Police, hosh mein aao (come to your senses),” he said.The video surfaces amid heightened security in Delhi for CJP’s ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Dahiya was removed as CJP spokesperson in July after videos of him at a burger outlet near a protest site drew criticism while party members and protesters were facing police action during the outfit’s ‘Chalo Sansad’ march.The party described his conduct as “deeply insensitive” and “unacceptable”, saying it was inconsistent with the movement’s values and principles. It also relieved him of all official duties.Dahiya defended his decision to eat at the outlet, saying he was hungry and had been working continuously for the movement.He questioned why eating a burger had become a major issue, arguing that people were overlooking the work done by those involved in the protest.Delhi Police detained more than 3,000 people across the capital as they attempted to reach Jantar Mantar for the proposed CJP demonstration. Detentions were reported near Regal Cinema, Minto Bridge and Akashwani Bhawan, among other locations.Police sources also said more than 600 people with criminal records were detained across Delhi as a preventive measure. Police had denied permission for the protest, citing public safety, traffic management and law-and-order concerns.Dipke, Das and Ranka were detained after arriving in Delhi from Mumbai. Rathee was also detained ahead of the planned demonstration.
Article Summary: Former Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Vijeta Dahiya mocks four detained party members. Dahiya was removed as CJP spokesperson in July after videos of him at a burger outlet near a protest site drew criticism. Police detained more than 3,000 people across the capital as they attempted to reach Jantar Mantar for the proposed demonstration.

Article Title: Industrialised personalisation
Article Text:
Industrialised personalisation, in the world of service, means a system set down so completely that anyone properly trained can replicate it and make an experience feel personal.

You have been inside the hotel for less than a minute when the waiter at the restaurant door greets you by name. Your usual table, the one by the window, is already laid. Before you open the menu the waiter asks whether it will be the sole again, as it was in March, and you, who eat out a good deal and are hard to impress, feel for a moment like the only guest in the building. You have not said anything. The waiter takes your coat with a small bow and leads the way.In 1911, Frederick Winslow Taylor's ‘The Principles of Scientific Management’ held that the best way to do each job should be worked out in advance, and taught. He wrote, “In the past the man has been first; in the future the system must be first.” Industrial production could then continue seamlessly, with each new worker fitting into the role with ease.The same logic had already moved from products into service, from Fred Harvey's railway restaurants in 1876 to White Castle's hamburger stands in 1921, and in 1948 the McDonald brothers rebuilt their restaurant around a nine-item menu and ran the kitchen like an assembly line. Let's follow a new hire called Dan on his first morning at the McDonald's on Sand Lake Road in Orlando, the chain’s largest outlet. For a moment he is overwhelmed by the arcade, ordering kiosks and a sea of impatient customers.The hour of briefing he was given steadies him. He matches each order number to its table, carries the tray over and says, as taught, “Have a nice meal!” In under a day few can tell he is new. This is industrialised industrialisation, with systems in place but execution still a little rough around the edges.In time, Dan moves to a job at a formal dining room where he trains for a whole week. He moves more fluidly now, personal worries don’t reflect in his demeanour, and his ‘thank you’ with a smile and a gentle nod sounds less rehearsed. The management has done its work well, and it takes a trained eye to see that his manner at the next table is no different.Attention reaches further at Eleven Madison Park, where, Will Guidara has said, whoever greeted you would have looked you up online beforehand. In ‘Unreasonable Hospitality’ he describes training the staff to set every plate so that in the event that a guest turned it over, he’d find the Limoges stamp facing him, right side up.At the Ritz-Carlton, Joseph Michelli reports, guest relations staff share news of arriving guests' anniversaries and celebrations at the daily lineup. You could arrive on a special day and find champagne, a handwritten card and pastries waiting in the room. The Ritz keeps the record of such care in Mystique, a database of guest preferences fed by notes that staff are trained to jot down. If you stayed at one of its hotels, the waiter would likely have drawn on it.Industrialised personalisation, in the world of service, means a system set down so completely that anyone properly trained can replicate it and make an experience feel personal.Dan leads you to the window. When the sole comes, it is cooked the way it was in March.
Article Summary: In 1911, Frederick Winslow Taylor's ‘The Principles of Scientific Management’ held that the best way to do each job should be worked out in advance, and taught. Industrial production could then continue seamlessly, with each new worker fitting into the role with ease. Industrialised personalisation means a system set down so completely that anyone properly trained can replicate it.

Article Title: Twenty-eight days in, the war began: Malaysia Airlines' CEO on fuel shocks, full planes and the India bet
Article Text:
Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar- President and Group Chief Executive Officer of Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG)

MUMBAI:

Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar- President and Group Chief Executive Officer of Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), took charge just before before the West Asia crisis began. Seven months on, he talks to the Times of India about running a thin-margin airline through a crisis, why India matters more than ever and what happens when the visa-free window closes.

The fuel bill nobody budgets for

India: The market that keeps filling up

Bilaterals and poor inbound traffic from Malaysia

The visa-free question

Profit, and the six-month check

The fleet is the bottleneck

Premium, food and crew

Selling the stopover

Lessons from the pandemic

Partners in code-share

A smarter airline

Nasaruddin A Bakar had barely found his CEO chair at Malaysia Aviation Group when the world's most important aviation corridor shut down."Twenty-eight days after I sat in the seat, the war started," the group CEO says, with the dry humour of a man who has since had time to reflect on it.The West Asia crisis that erupted at the end of February did what such conflicts do to airlines. It closed airspace, stranded passengers, and sent fuel prices soaring. Eight months on, fuel prices are nowhere near cooling. For the new CEO, the first month was about survival and logistics rather than strategy."The first two weeks were about how we manage three things: our people over there, our passengers over there, and our assets in the Middle East," he says. He spent much of that time with his team, trying to understand what was happening on the ground."War happens every time. What strikes an airline most is when the fuel price goes up, and in those first forty days or so of the war, it was very critical."He puts numbers on it. Fuel typically accounts for about 40 per cent of Malaysia Airlines' total operating cost. During the conflict, that share rose to nearly 55 or 56 per cent.For an airline already operating on slender margins, that is a brutal swing. He said the margin across the Asia-Pacific region averages only about 2 per cent. "If you sell $100, you only make $2 in profit. When something happens in some part of the world, that margin is gone."The Gulf's loss was Kuala Lumpur's gain, at least for a while. With the Middle East hubs disrupted, travellers who would normally have connected through the Gulf looked for other routes. Many of them, especially those travelling between Australia, New Zealand and Europe, turned to Southeast Asia."Kuala Lumpur and Singapore, in particular, saw a big increase in demand, and we increased our frequencies and our flights into London," he says. Load factors on those flights touched 95, 99 and even 100 per cent.That surge has since cooled. Demand plateaued around June or July, he says, because many of those who wanted to move had already done so. It is still strong, though. Loads to Europe remain in the high 80s to around 90 per cent.This is the first time in over two decades that he has visited Mumbai. Last time around, he had flown in as a pilot-in-command. When asked about the purpose of his visit, he said: "India is one of the biggest economies in the world, and I think India is the right market to go to."The numbers back him up. Malaysia Airlines operates about 80 flights a week to India, including 12 a week to Chennai, and flies to ten Indian destinations, among them both metros and second-tier cities. The airline carried about 1.3 million passengers on its India routes in the first half of 2025. Passenger growth in India is running at roughly 11 per cent year on year, and by the end of July the airline had already flown close to one million passengers on its India routes this year, he said.The planes are almost full. "Fortunately, or unfortunately, our load factor is right to the brim now." Loads on India routes average around 93 per cent. He cites 93 per cent in Chennai, 91 per cent in Mumbai and 91 to 92 per cent in most other cities, which he says makes India one of the highest-loading foreign markets in the network.How much of that traffic is bound for Malaysia? About 70 per cent of passengers from India travel onwards through Kuala Lumpur, and only about 30 per cent fly point to point. Most of the onward traffic is headed to Australia, mainly Sydney and Melbourne, with a smaller share going to Japan and very little to China, he said.That makes KL a hub in the true sense of the word, a role Capt Nasa is keen to push. “Kuala Lumpur is the fourth most connected hub in the world, ahead of Singapore and Bangkok,” he said. OAG data released in Sept put Istanbul airport at the first place globally with connections to 337 destinations worldwide, followed by London Heathrow and Amsterdam Schiphol in the third place. Kuala Lumpur retained its fourth position and remains the most connected airport in Asia, with destinations served increasing to 154.The imbalance in India-Malaysia passenger traffic is stark, too. By his estimate, about 750,000 Indians travel to Malaysia, against roughly 200,000 Malaysians going the other way. That lop-sidedness is one reason capacity is hard to add. India's bilateral air services agreement caps what each side's carriers can fly, and Malaysia Airlines shares its Malaysian quota with AirAsia and Batik."Our work, through our government, is always about asking whether we can get more bilateral arrangements," he says. "The process is ongoing, and we have asked many times." He says he understands the position on both sides.Much of that growth in outbound traffic from India to Malaysia has come with a tailwind: Malaysia's visa-free regime for Indian travellers. It is due to lapse in December. He did not comment on whether it will be extended. "Our government-to-government relationship between Malaysia and India has been very strong, and I believe the visa-free arrangement benefits both countries."Malaysia has declared 2026 as Visit Malaysia Year, and the airline's own targets look to the same horizon. "We are looking at maybe two to three million tourists from India alone this year, across all carriers," he says. For an airline whose Indian planes are already nearly full, that number may be as much a message to the Malaysian government as a forecast.In April, the airline announced a profit of USD 34 million for 2025, roughly double the previous years. The CEO’s message back then was celebratory but cautious. He warned about volatility and geopolitics.So, six months on, which pressures have turned out to be more persistent or more severe than expected? The CEO said the first two months of the year were profitable and strong, financially, and operationally. Then he moved quickly to what he considers the airline's real achievement. Its on-time performance is running at 92 to 94 percent. "We are not only ensuring that we fly from A to B. We are selling an experience."He is clear-eyed about the ambition behind that. Malaysia Airlines now ranks 21st on Skytrax, up from 26th, and he wants it in the top ten within four years. "Can it be achieved? Obviously, it can."The more stubborn problem is supply. The airline ordered 95 aircraft three years ago and has received 29 so far. Another 66 are due over the next four years. Delays of three to five months are routine."I don't see the supply chain being resolved in the next five years, at least," he says. "I'm praying so hard for that, but looking at the trend, it might even take longer."For a small airline, the cost is high. Malaysia Airlines has already sold about 25 percent of its 2027 seats, he said. "If a flight is delayed by three months, a small airline like us has a big problem," he says. He is frank about the manufacturers. "We're trying our level best, and the manufacturers say they are doing theirs, but to me their level best is not good enough."The average age of the fleet is 10.3 years. He wants to bring it down to 5.7 by 2030, since about 75 per cent of the new order is replacement and only a quarter is growth. A decision on long-range widebody aircraft is expected within a month or two.“We should be announcing our white body replacement maybe next month or before year end, the replacement of our A350 aircraft, which is about nine years old today,” he said.When asked whether a passenger flying in 2030 can be sure of a fresh cabin, he declined to promise. "Nothing is certain. You will always have some aircraft that are ten years old. But I'm talking about the average."Capt Nasa describes the airline's long-term business plan, now in its third edition, as resting on four pillars: being a premium carrier, building partnerships, achieving operational excellence, and strengthening its non-airline businesses. Traffic isn’t the only goal. "We want to be known as a premium carrier, so everything we do is about driving premiumness, not just traffic."On the customer side, he narrows it to three things. The first is the cabin: new aircraft and, as importantly, cabins that work well.The second is food. "Malaysians love to eat, and Indians love to eat too," he says. He has added 30 menus in the last nine months, and the flight he took to India the day before the interview was serving an Indian menu. The airline will also build its own catering facility, with ground-breaking in July, to produce around 60,000 meals a day by 2028, selling the surplus to other airlines.When told that a passenger flying on a Malaysian carrier might prefer Malaysian food, he conceded the point but said the airline's own analysis shows that most customers want something familiar. So Indian food it is.The third is hospitality. “Malaysia Airlines' cabin crew have won a world's-best award seven times, and this year they are ranked third on Skytrax,” he said. The airline last topped the list about 18 years ago, and he believes it is on a path back to number one.Because most Indian passengers are in transit, Malaysia Airlines has a product to coax them off the plane: the bonus side trip. A traveller who stops in Kuala Lumpur gets a free ticket to a second destination, a domestic destination."Say you are going to Japan. The price flying direct is one figure and the price through Kuala Lumpur is another, but we say, come through us and I will give you one ticket free to Langkawi."The offer has grown from six destinations to eight, including Kuching, Penang, Johor Bahru and Langkawi. It was introduced two or three years ago and is aimed at leisure travellers rather than corporate ones, who want to get to Australia, Japan etc directly, he said. The share of passengers who use it is small though, but it helps to sell, he added.On pricing, he insists the airline competes on something other than fares. "It is important for us to sell the experience. It is not about the price." Dynamic pricing, he adds, means early buyers can find fares cheaper than some competitors.“The learnings that we got from COVID is this. As an airline, you cannot put everything under one basket. So, when we restructured the company in 2023, we diversified our businesses. We've got airline business, we've got non-airline businesses, we want to be strong and to be resilient in our non-airline businesses,” he said. From the Indian market point of view, the airline sees cargo and MRO businesses as strong segments.With around 18,000 aircraft backlogged at manufacturers, airlines are extending leases, and that means more heavy checks, he said, adding that no Indian airline sends aircraft to Malaysia Airlines' MRO arm today. But he sees it as a chance, since the group works on both Boeing and Airbus. When told, India has long complained about losing maintenance business abroad, his answer was diplomatic: "To me, the cake is so big that everyone can have a portion. " Cargo and MRO are two of the group's six non-airline businesses, along with loyalty, catering, ground handling and a training academy.Malaysia Airlines has a codeshare with IndiGo on six Indian domestic points and a joint business agreement with Singapore Airlines. It is also a Oneworld member, though that alliance has no Indian carrier. The CEO did not have passenger numbers for the IndiGo tie-up. “In terms of the number, it is steadily improving. It is not there yet, but we need it, we want it to be much better.”IndiGo's push into long-haul does not worry him unduly. Thirty or forty years ago, he notes, Southeast Asia and India had only six or seven airlines, and now there are more than 50. "Competition is stiff, but the market has grown a lot." He expects the Asia-Pacific region to grow six to seven per cent a year for the next 20 years, against about four per cent globally. "Of course, it is a concern to us. Even though the market is big, we have to be very smart. "Technology, too, is on his list, as is with most airline CEOs. About 75 per cent of customers now start their search on Google or an AI tool, and about 20 percent of those convert into a ticket, he said. Malaysia Airlines runs 49 AI platforms across its operations, from flight planning to disruption management. Citing an example, he talks about rebooking disrupted passengers, where the system can use customer data to decide who goes on which flight, such as sending someone bound for London directly rather than through KL.
Article Summary: Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar is the President and Group Chief Executive Officer of Malaysia Aviation Group. Fuel typically accounts for about 40 per cent of Malaysia Airlines' total operating cost. The airline carried about 1.3 million passengers on its India routes in the first half of 2025.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent slips as Trump cites 'productive talks' with Iran
Article Text:
Brent crude futures fell 72 cents, or 0.7%, to $103.53 a barrel.

Oil prices fell on Friday as concerns over Middle East supply disruptions eased after US President Donald Trump said Washington would not attack Iran before next month's US elections. He also cited progress in talks aimed at ending the conflict, which has disrupted global oil markets.Brent crude futures fell 72 cents, or 0.7%, to $103.53 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 52 cents, or 0.6%, to $90.97 by 7:50 am IST.Despite Friday's decline, Brent was on track for a weekly gain after settling 4% higher on Thursday amid increased attacks earlier this week on vessels carrying crude oil out of the Middle East.WTI, however, was set for a slight weekly decline despite supply disruptions caused by a hurricane approaching the US Gulf Coast.Earlier on Thursday, Trump said Washington was having “productive discussions” with Iran and that no attack was planned before the November 3 US midterm congressional elections. His remarks came after media reports suggested he was considering military action before the polls.Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days.The US continues to apply economic pressure on Iran in an effort to end the conflict, which is now in its eighth month.On Thursday, Washington imposed fresh sanctions targeting individuals, networks and 17 vessels allegedly involved in transporting Iranian crude oil, petroleum products and petrochemicals.Oil prices have fluctuated this week amid growing threats to shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. Before the war, the strategic waterway handled shipments equivalent to about 20% of global oil and fuel supplies.Oil markets are also monitoring Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf of Mexico. The storm has forced producers to shut in about 1.3 million barrels per day, or 62.9% of current oil production in the region, as of Thursday, according to the US Marine Minerals Administration.Oil markets have remained unsettled for more than seven months since the conflict in the Middle East began. Despite the latest gains, prices remain below the $126-a-barrel level reached earlier in the crisis.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 72 cents, or 0.7%, to $103.53 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures declined 52 cents, to $90.97 by 7:50 am IST. Despite Friday's decline, Brent was on track for a weekly gain after settling 4% higher on Thursday.

Article Title: Major crackdown on Green Cards: What is PERM program & which IT firms has US suspended
Article Text:
Vance singled out Microsoft, accusing it of laying off 6,000 American workers in 2025

Microsoft Adobe Cognizant Infosys Tata Wipro HCL Capgemini

What is PERM visa and how does it work?

The US has suspended eight major technology companies, including Microsoft, Tata, Infosys and Wipro, from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme, in a major crackdown on the use of foreign workers for jobs that the government says could be filled by Americans. The move was announced by Vice President JD Vance, Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling and Attorney General Todd Blanche under the US Anti-Fraud Task Force.The Department of Labour said it would not accept new or process pending PERM applications involving the companies. Sonderling said the firms alone had requested almost three million foreign workers since 2009, securing more than 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications.Vance singled out Microsoft, accusing it of laying off 6,000 American workers in 2025 while obtaining more than 6,000 H-1B approvals and filing 3,682 PERM applications. "Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers in 2025 after certifying that it could not find qualified American employees," Vance said.Which IT firms are suspended from PERM programme:Sonderling said the suspensions covered some of the world's largest IT outsourcing companies.He said Microsoft and Adobe were being suspended due to multiple active federal investigations, while the other firms were also targeted as part of the broader crackdown.Indian professionals account for more than 70% of approved H-1B petitions annually, making the move particularly significant for Indian technology workers seeking permanent residency in the US.PERM, or Permanent Labour Certification, is not itself a visa. It is a labour certification process administered by the US Department of Labour that is required for most employment-based green card applications.Under the system, a US employer must establish that there are not enough qualified, willing and available American workers for a particular job, and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed US workers.The process generally begins with the employer identifying a permanent, full-time position and determining its minimum requirements and duties. The employer then obtains a prevailing wage determination from the Department of Labour.The employer must also complete the required recruitment and notification process to demonstrate that it has sought qualified US workers. After completing these steps, it submits the PERM application to the Department of Labour, usually through the online FLAG system. If the labour certification is approved, the employer can use it as a step towards filing the relevant employment-based immigrant petition with US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).
Article Summary: The US has suspended eight major technology companies, including Microsoft, Tata, Infosys and Wipro. The move was announced by Vice President JD Vance, Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling and Attorney General Todd Blanche. The Department of Labour said it would not accept new or process pending PERM applications involving the companies.

Article Title: US visa chaos: Tata, Wipro among IT firms suspended from PERM scheme; what it means
Article Text:
The PERM programme is a key step in the employment-based green card process

What is the PERM programme

How PERM was meant to protect US workers

NEW DELHI: The Trump administration has stepped up its crackdown on the US immigration system, suspending major technology companies including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, Capgemini and HCL from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme amid allegations of abuse of H-1B visas and the employment of foreign workers.US Vice President JD Vance accused Microsoft of laying off thousands of American workers while simultaneously benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and green cards. The administration has also put nine universities under investigation over alleged misuse of visa-related programmes, adding to growing uncertainty for foreign workers and international students in the US.Announcing Microsoft's suspension from the PERM programme, Vance said the company had laid off 6,000 American workers while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards."There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft."“If you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants,” Vance said at a White House news conference.Vance also accused companies of using foreign workers to undercut American employees, saying: "This is a fundamental INSULT to the American worker and to the American way of life. We CANNOT allow visa programs that were designed to ensure that American corporations had access to the best and the brightest, to use them to undercut the wages of American workers!"The Permanent Labour Certification programme, or PERM, is a Department of Labour process that allows US employers to seek certification to permanently employ foreign workers.Under the process, employers generally have to demonstrate that there are not enough able, willing, qualified and available US workers for the job and that hiring a foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed American workers.Once the labour certification is approved by the Department of Labour, the employer can proceed with an immigrant petition to the US Citizenship and Immigration Services, generally through Form I-140.For H-1B workers, PERM can therefore form an important step in the employment-based green card process. Suspending a company's access to the programme can make it harder for the company to sponsor eligible foreign workers for permanent residence.The PERM programme is designed to ensure that American workers are not disadvantaged when employers seek to hire foreign workers for permanent jobs. Before sponsoring a foreign worker for a green card, an employer generally has to demonstrate that there are not enough qualified, willing and available US workers for the position and that hiring the foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed Americans.The concern for US authorities arises when employers manipulate or bypass this labour-market test. Fraudulent recruitment can make it appear that no suitable American worker is available when, in reality, qualified US workers may have been discouraged from applying or effectively excluded from consideration. The Department of Labor's inspector general has identified vulnerabilities in the PERM system, including concerns over fraudulent applications, inadequate supporting documentation and weaknesses in post-certification enforcement.Wages are another concern. Employers are required to meet prevailing wage requirements, which are intended to prevent foreign-worker hiring from depressing wages for American workers in comparable jobs. If employers circumvent these requirements or use arrangements that effectively reduce the foreign worker's compensation, the government says the system can undermine the safeguards built into PERM.The administration's latest moves have also extended beyond companies. The Department of Homeland Security has proposed a $70,000 fee for international students participating in the Optional Practical Training programme, which allows eligible foreign students to work in jobs related to their studies.
Article Summary: The Trump administration has stepped up its crackdown on the US immigration system. It has suspended major technology companies including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, Capgemini and HCL from the Permanent Labour Certification programme. The administration has also put nine universities under investigation over alleged misuse of visa-related programmes.

Article Title: AI could turn fresh finance hires into managers from day one: Goldman Sachs
Article Text:
AI could make young finance hires managers from day one

What will young hires do

Traditional career ladder may change

Banks may need fewer fresh graduates

As artificial intelligence advances, young finance professionals may no longer have to spend years waiting for their first management role.With AI taking on more work, new hires could find themselves managing AI agents from the start of their careers, according to Goldman Sachs executive Kevin Sneader.Sneader, who leads Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s business in Asia Pacific outside Japan, said that the shift could also raise questions about the future role of middle managers, who have traditionally taken on management responsibilities after years of experience.“When our young folks now start work, they’re managing agents,” Sneader said on Thursday at the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore. “They have to make the most of this virtual army that they’ve now got.”Bloomberg Previous generations often spent years in their jobs before getting the opportunity to manage anyone. But as AI changes the way work is done, management responsibilities could move closer to the front line.“That management task no longer sits with the middle manager; it sits with the front line,” Sneader said. “We don’t quite know what’s going to happen to that group.”Sneader said re-deploying existing managers would be the “generational challenge for many, many segments”.The comments point to a possible change in the traditional banking career path, where junior employees spend years working on analysis and preparatory tasks before moving into management roles.Rather than focusing on mass job losses from AI, Sneader and other panellists discussing AI and finance focused on how jobs and responsibilities could be reshaped.Sandra Peterson, an operating partner at investment firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, said the traditional career ladder in professional services may not survive in the same form.“It used to be that professional service firms were pyramids,” she said. “You’d show up, and you know, you march your way through, and if you survived, you got to the next level, the next level, the next level.”With AI doing much of the grunt work, Peterson said it was unclear whether firms would need as many entry-level positions.Singapore’s financial regulator is also seeing changes in how jobs could be organised. Chia Der Jiun, managing director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, said operations staff would need to become managers and supervisors of AI agents.Banks would also need fewer fresh graduates for analysis and preparatory work, he said.Singapore has been preparing for these changes by training bank staff in AI skills and working with universities to ensure its graduates are ready for the new world, Chia said.For young people, Sneader said the opportunities could extend beyond finding a job in finance.“There’s never been a better time to be an entrepreneur to create something,” he said, noting that fewer resources are needed to start a business nowadays.“That’s quite an exciting part of the future when we’re all spending too much time, perhaps worrying about the old world.
Article Summary: New hires could find themselves managing AI agents from the start of their careers, says Goldman Sachs executive Kevin Sneader. Previous generations often spent years in their jobs before getting the opportunity to manage anyone. Sneader said re-deploying existing managers would be the “generational challenge for many, many segments”

Article Title: Russia eyes return to Europe's gas market despite sanctions, Ukraine war: Report
Article Text:
Russia aims to reach Europe’s gas market through Nord Stream pipeline (Representational image)

Nord Stream back on the table

Restarting gas flows won't be easy

Germany split over Russian gas

Who owns Nord Stream?

Lukoil assets also in focus

Russia may be looking to turn the gas taps to Europe back on, with talks under way over bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that once carried Russian gas to Germany.According to five people familiar with the matter, the discussions involve US Special Envoy Jared Kushner and Kirill Dmitriev, a close adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin.Kushner, who has been trying to broker a truce between Russia and Ukraine, sees business deals as central to restoring peace. A potential Nord Stream deal could allow US investors to profit from energy flows to Europe once the war ends.Kushner and Dmitriev have met in Moscow and New York in recent weeks. Two sources told Reuters that Nord Stream remains on the agenda, although not much details are available about the discussions.Dmitriev, who has been pushing for Russian gas sales to Germany to resume, met representatives of the US energy and treasury departments last month, to discuss potential US-Russia energy initiatives.A White House official said that any deals would have to be negotiated with the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and Treasury and must benefit US taxpayers and companies."Any deals will have to be negotiated by Russia with DFC (US International Development Finance Corporation) and Treasury and must benefit United States taxpayers and companies," the official said.The official also said there had been "no Nord Stream discussions recently".A return of Russian gas to Germany still faces several hurdles. The Nord Stream pipelines are sanctioned by the US and the EU, making any restart illegal.A US official said a deal was unlikely in the medium term because of the obstacles involved. US President Donald Trump could waive or soften US sanctions, but that would become harder if Democrats win control of Congress in next month's midterm elections.Germany and other European countries are also expected to oppose reopening Nord Stream. They are spending billions of euros rebuilding their military to defend themselves from Russia.A spokeswoman for Germany's economy and energy ministry said Nord Stream and Russian gas were sanctioned in Europe and that Germany had found alternatives. She said reopening the pipelines would require government approval and was not desired.Before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Germany bought more than half of its gas from Russia through the two Nord Stream pipelines. They were mothballed after Moscow throttled supplies to Europe and were blown up in a series of underwater explosions in September 2022.The idea of bringing Russian gas back to Germany has also divided opinion within the country.Germany's coalition government is opposed to restarting the pipeline, while Alternative for Germany (AfD), the country's most popular political party, wants to reopen it. Dmitriev is due to meet AfD leadership early next year to discuss selling Russian gas again.Poland is also watching the discussions but remains firmly opposed to reopening the pipeline, according to one person familiar with the government's thinking. Poland and the Baltic states are particularly vulnerable to Russia and reject energy ties.The talks are taking place against a backdrop of deep European mistrust of Russia's motives. Earlier this year, the heads of five European spy agencies told Reuters that Russia did not want to end the war quickly and was using US talks to push for business deals instead.Relations between Russia and Germany, which is among the biggest providers of military support to Ukraine, have hit a low ebb. Officials in Berlin have accused Russia of mounting a systematic campaign of hybrid attacks.Some German lawmakers say business deals would bolster Moscow as it pursues war with Ukraine."This threatens to be a dirty deal that will cost Europe dearly," said Michael Kellner, a lawmaker who was in charge of German energy policy in the aftermath of the Ukraine invasion."Americans and Russians will share the profits," he said.Ownership could be another hurdle for any US investment in Nord Stream.Russian state energy giant Gazprom owns 51% of the company. Another 31% is split between two German entities, while the remaining stake is held by a French and a Dutch firm.The two German shareholders want to retain their stakes to maintain German influence if Gazprom sells its share, another person familiar with the matter said.Days after the Moscow meetings, Kushner said in Kyiv that he had spoken to European counterparts about how the war had pushed up energy prices. He advocated "prosperity agreements" to encourage peace and give "leaders ... something to look forward to".Kushner and Dmitriev have also discussed the possible sale of businesses owned by Russian energy company Lukoil, including oil refineries and petrol stations in Europe and elsewhere, two people familiar with the matter said.Under the proposal, a consortium involving the DFC and investors from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates would buy the assets, while US authorities would lift sanctions, the people said."On Lukoil, Steve (Witkoff) and Jared (Kushner) worked with DFC to negotiate a substantial upfront payment and profits interest for the United States," a White House official said.
Article Summary: Talks under way over bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that once carried Russian gas to Germany. US Special Envoy Jared Kushner sees business deals as central to restoring peace. A potential Nord Stream deal could allow US investors to profit from energy flows to Europe.

Article Title: US mortgage rates jump to 7.49%, hit highest level in nearly 3 years
Article Text:
US mortgage rate climbs to three year high

US mortgage rates have soared to their highest level in nearly three years, with the sharp rise in borrowing costs adding to pressure on the housing market as Americans head towards November 3 elections.The average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) said, as cited by Reuters. This spike pushed rates to the highest level since November 2023, hitting demand for home loans.Mortgage applications dropped 4.2% last week from the previous week, while refinancing applications fell sharply. Overall application volumes are now at their lowest since February 2025 and have declined nearly 50% since January."Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist told Reuters.Mortgage rates have closely followed movements in the yield on 10-year US treasury notes. Earlier this week, the yield topped 5.3%, reaching a 24-year high, with concerns over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth driving the rise.Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar increase in the 10-year treasury yield.The increase comes at a politically sensitive time, with the US mid-term elections just four weeks away. The cost of living was the top issue among Americans in deciding how they would vote, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday. At the same time, US President Donald Trump's approval rating stood at a record low of 32%.Inflation has also risen, reaching 3.4% in August on a measure targeted by the Federal Reserve at 2%.Fed policymakers have signalled that they expect another interest-rate increase by the end of the year following the rate hike in September. Markets are currently betting that policymakers will not raise rates at the next meeting at the end of October.The latest increase in mortgage rates comes as affordability remains under pressure for buyers, while the decline in loan applications points to weaker activity in the mortgage market.
Article Summary: US mortgage rates have soared to their highest level in nearly three years. The average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose 19 basis points to 7.49%. This spike pushed rates to the highest level since November 2023, hitting demand for home loans.

Article Title: Oil remains beyond $100 per barrel as Middle East supply concerns persist
Article Text:
Crude oil prices continue to rally

Oil prices inched higher on Thursday as concerns over supply from the Middle East intensified amid a rise in attacks on vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude was trading at $101.50 a barrel, up $1.32 or 1.32%, while WTI crude stood at $89.28, gaining $1 or 1.13%.The latest gains come despite a fall in prices in the previous session, when the International Energy Agency agreed to speed up the release of oil stocks and give priority to diesel supplies. The plan, launched in March, is aimed at dealing with record fuel prices and supply disruptions linked to the Iran war.Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has become a growing concern as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran enters its eighth month. Before the war, the route handled shipments equivalent to about 20% of global oil and fuel supplies.The pressure on shipping has increased even as Gulf producers raise exports. Tanker attacks through the Strait reached their highest level last week for any week since the Iran war began, leaving crude shipments facing higher costs and greater risks for cargoes and crew.A tanker north of Qatar was struck by multiple projectiles in the latest attack, causing casualties, the United Kingdom maritime trade operations agency said on Wednesday.Supply concerns were accompanied by signs of tighter US inventories. According to Reuters, American crude stocks fell by 3.2 million barrels in the week ended October 2 to 424.1 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration. The decline was larger than the 1.7 million-barrel fall analysts had expected in a Reuters poll.Diesel and jet fuel inventories also declined, with distillate fuel stocks falling by 42,000 barrels to 105.14 million barrels. Those inventories remained below their levels for this period of the year over the past five years.Oil markets have remained unsettled for more than seven months since the Middle East conflict began. Even with the latest increase, prices are still below the $126 a barrel level reached earlier in the crisis.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $101.50 a barrel, up $1.32 or 1.32%. WTI crude stood at $89.28, gaining $1 or1.13%. The latest gains come despite a fall in prices in the previous session.

Article Title: Iraq’s dinar takes a hit as official rate resets, market rate crosses 1,700
Article Text:
Iraq devalues its currency

Iraq’s dinar has taken a step down against the US dollar, with the country officially resetting its exchange rate from around 1,300 dinars to 1,500 dinars per dollar. But in the market, the dollar is already fetching more than 1,700 dinars.The new official rate was decided at a Cabinet meeting on Tuesday night, according to Iraq’s central bank, which said the move was made “to meet the relevant financial, economic and monetary requirements.”The previous official exchange rate had been set in 2023. In practice, however, Iraq has always had a difference between the official rate and the rate used by exchange shops. That gap had widened in recent months, with the unofficial rate crossing 1,600 dinars to the dollar even before the official devaluation.After the new official rate was announced, the market rate climbed further to more than 1,700 dinars per dollar.The widening gap has come amid the US-Iran war, which has at times spilled over into Iraq, and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Iraq’s economy relies heavily on oil exports, most of which were shipped through the strait before the war. Since the war began, Iraq has shifted to sending oil overland through Syria for export, a route that is more expensive and less efficient.Under the new official rate, Iraq’s Finance Ministry will sell dollars at 1,500 dinars per dollar, while consumers buying dollars from banks will pay 1,520 dinars per dollar.
Article Summary: Iraq devalues its dinar against the US dollar. The new official rate is 1,500 dinars per dollar. But in the market, the dollar is already fetching more than 1,700 dinars. The widening gap has come amid the US-Iran war and disruptions to shipping.

Article Title: Amazon Prime becomes 'permanent home' for Emmy Awards as 'Wheel Deal' system ends
Article Text:
Emmys shift from 'Wheel Deal' to Amazon Prime

The Emmys are leaving their decades-old broadcast TV rotation behind, with Amazon’s Prime Video set to become the awards show’s exclusive global streaming home from 2027.The Television Academy and Amazon announced a six-year agreement on Tuesday that will make the ceremony available live and free to audiences in more than 240 countries and territories. Furthermore, viewers will not need a Prime Video subscription to watch the show.The ceremony will continue to take place in September, with Prime Video’s rights beginning with the 2027 edition. NBC, owned by Comcast, aired this year’s ceremony on September 14.The deal brings an end to the “Wheel Deal” system under which ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC took turns broadcasting the Emmys. The arrangement has been in place since at least 1994, with the latest eight-year contract expiring this year.Prime Video has been named the “permanent home” of the Emmys in the announcement, marking a departure from the awards show’s long-running practice of moving between the four US broadcast networks.“Television has never been more global, and the Emmys should be a celebration that the world can share,” Television Academy chair Cris Abrego said in a statement.“Having a dedicated home with Prime Video allows us to build on that legacy with unprecedented global reach and a broader commitment to the Television Academy and our mission throughout the year,” he said.The financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed.The move comes as streaming services take a larger role in live television, while traditional broadcast and cable networks face increasing competition as viewing habits shift towards streaming subscriptions. Major entertainment and sports events have increasingly moved to or added streaming platforms, including events whose rights were previously held exclusively by traditional networks.The Emmys' move is also part of a wider shift among major US awards shows. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced in December 2025 that Alphabet’s YouTube and YouTube TV would take over media rights to the Oscars from ABC in 2029. Netflix has exclusively aired the SAG Awards since 2024.For Amazon, the agreement adds a major live entertainment event to Prime Video’s existing offering of original films and television programmes, sports and other streaming partnerships.First held in 1949, the Emmy Awards recognise achievements in television acting, production and writing, among other categories. The ceremony has traditionally been a major promotional and cultural event for the US television industry.
Article Summary: The Emmys are leaving their decades-old broadcast TV rotation behind. Amazon's Prime Video will become the awards show's exclusive global streaming home from 2027. The deal brings an end to the “Wheel Deal’ system under which ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC took turns broadcasting the Emmys.

Article Title: Brent crosses $101 as Saudi attacks, US storm add to oil supply concerns
Article Text:
Brent crosses $101 once again

Oil prices rose more than 1% on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing the $101-a-barrel mark as fresh supply risks outweighed rising optimism due to increased Middle East crude supplies.WTI crude rose 1.05% to $90.38 a barrel, while Brent crude gained 1.02% to $101.60 as supply concerns emerged in Saudi Arabia and the US oil and refining sector.The latest concerns came from both sides of the global oil supply chain. According to US forecasters, a storm developing in the Gulf of Mexico is expected to become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days and is likely to affect oil and gas facilities.The areas in the storm's path account for 15% of US crude production and 5% of the country's natural gas production. Six refineries could also be affected. Refineries located in US Gulf states represent about 50% of the country's total refining capacity of 18.2 million barrels per day (bpd).The prospect of disruption has emerged even as oil supplies from the Middle East have increased.
